item.title: Allianz backs Dili
item.description: Allianz participated in a $15 million Series A for Dili , an AI-powered compliance platform serving energy, infrastructure, construction and manufacturing projects. The financing brings Dili’s total funding to $21.7 million. Founded in 2023 by Anand Chaturvedi and Brian Fernandez, New York-based Dili automates prevailing-wage monitoring, apprenticeship compliance, certified-payroll reviews and audit reporting.

item.title: AXA is done fixing margins
item.description: AXA is done fixing P&C margins and wants growth Management believes profitability in retail and commercial P&C, excluding AXA XL, is already at an excellent level. AXA intends to preserve those margins while using favorable pricing conditions to add business. “With profitability at excellent level, we do not see the need to improve margins further.

item.title: Everest has walked away from more than $1 billion of casualty business
item.description: Everest has walked away from more than $1 billion of casualty business Everest continues to shrink casualty where pricing, structure or expected returns do not meet its requirements. Management said the company has withdrawn from more than $1 billion of casualty business over the past several quarters. “Our third-party capital platform, Mount Logan Capital Management, has approximately $3.4 billion of AUM as of July 1, up 89% from the beginning of 2025.” Buybacks have reduced the share count by more than 10% Everest has spent $1.5 billion repurchasing shares since Jim Williamson became CEO in January 2025.

item.title: Bring It On: AI Strategy Sways Underwriter Choices of Employers
item.description: Now, according to a recent survey, nearly three-quarters say they’re opting for companies with clear AI strategies as employers. Specifically, according to the report based on the responses of underwriters and executives who are mainly involved in writing commercial P/C lines of insurance, 72% said a structured AI strategy would matter to them when considering new roles. item.title: YASSI Launches Vehicle Intelligence API
item.description: (Image source: YASSI website.) Yotta Automated Software Solutions (YASSI; Santa Rosa, Calif.) has launched Easy-Connect API, an enterprise vehicle intelligence platform for insurers, lenders, automotive retailers, fleet operators and government agencies. The API gives enterprise customers access to real-time vehicle intelligence through a single integration, according to a YASSI statement. “Enterprise vehicle intelligence has to perform at scale, integrate seamlessly, and protect sensitive data without compromise,” comments Patrick Brown, CTO and Co-Founder, YASSI.

item.title: Bestow Launches AI Lab for Life Insurers
item.description: (Image source: Bestow website.) Bestow (Dallas) has launched Bestow Labs, a dedicated team focused on developing AI-native products for the life and annuity insurance industry. The company says Bestow Labs will pursue AI-native solutions for insurers while operating separately from Bestow’s production systems, allowing experimentation without affecting the regulated infrastructure carriers use today. The launch comes as Bestow expands its platform across the life and annuity insurance lifecycle, including new business, policy administration and digital purchase experiences.

item.title: Plutus Launches Life, Annuity AI Platform
item.description: (Image source: Plutus website.) Plutus (Chicago) has launched the Plutus Agentic Platform for Life and Annuity Operations, a set of AI-assisted workflow solutions built natively inside ServiceNow (Santa Clara, Calif.). The platform includes six purpose-built solutions for life and annuity carriers, organized around transaction processing, operational controls and book-level remediation, according to a Plutus statement. The Plutus Agentic Platform for Life and Annuity Operations is available now for pilot deployments in the ServiceNow ecosystem.

item.title: Tesla Faces US Auto Safety Probe Over Risk of Suspension Failure
item.description: auto safety regulators opened an investigation into Tesla Inc.’s most-popular models after a series of complaints by drivers over the sudden failure of suspension in their vehicles. Related: Tesla’s Cratering Cybertruck Sales Evoke Ford Edsel Comparisons Drivers in the cited incidents said there was typically no advance warning before the suspension failure, though some reported hearing unusual noises. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has received 156 reports of apparent suspension issues in Teslas, which “potentially causes a loss of vehicle directional control,” according to documents posted to the agency’s website Friday.

item.title: eBay Agreed to Pay Nearly $50M to Couple Sent Cockroaches, Bloody Pig Mask
item.description: agreed to pay almost $50 million to a Massachusetts couple who said former employees of the company targeted them with threats and bizarre anonymous deliveries — including live insects, a funeral wreath and a bloody pig Halloween mask, according to settlement details released Tuesday. Ina Steiner said the campaign began with threatening direct messages on social media before escalating into anonymous deliveries of live cockroaches and spiders, a funeral wreath, a bloody pig Halloween mask and a book about surviving the death of a spouse. The employees also sent pornographic magazines with David Steiner’s name to a neighbor’s home and planned to install a GPS device on the couple’s car.

item.title: Cargo Theft Tactics Changing, Expert Says
item.description: Cargo theft is no longer just a physical security problem, according to Michael Fisk, vice president of Roadmaster Group and a senior leader at Tri-State Motor Transit Co. “What we’re seeing is a fundamental change in how cargo theft works,” said Fisk. Organized criminal networks are deliberately shifting away from smash-and-grab tactics toward identity fraud and document forgery.

item.title: Driver Death Rates High for Small Cars, Big Engines: IIHS
item.description: More than half of the model 2023 vehicles with the highest driver death rates are small cars, sports cars, or muscle cars, according to a new report from the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety. They’re dangerous mainly because of how they’re driven.” IIHS has been calculating driver death rates approximately every three years since 1989. Eighteen out of the 20 models with the lowest driver death rates are SUVs, including four small, nine midsize, four large and one very large model.

item.title: Data center exposure requires blend of insurance, reinsurance, ILS capital: Gallagher Securities CEO
item.description: Bolding, who serves as CEO of Gallagher Securities, the insurance-linked securities (ILS) and capital markets broker-dealer division of reinsurance broker Gallagher Re, recently spoke to Artemis about the necessity for increased risk capital to facilitate the development of data centers, and how ILS can play a crucial role in this process. In light of this, Jason Bolding from Gallagher Securities has emphasised that the growth will require a blend of traditional insurance, reinsurance, captives, catastrophe bonds, and sidecars to effectively fill the widening protection gap. “Data center exposure is becoming too large for traditional insurance capacity alone, and the industry will need additional sources of capital.

item.title: Run-off deal volumes fall in H1 2026 despite steady underlying demand: PwC
item.description: PwC concludes that the combination of a softening underwriting cycle, unresolved casualty reserve uncertainty, tightening reinsurance returns and broader structural change within the legacy market together point towards a sector well placed to sustain meaningful run-off deal activity through the remainder of 2026 and into 2027. Looking at the first half of the year overall, PwC notes that the total of 13 disclosed deals falls short of the 23 seen across the same period in 2025, and that the estimated $780 million of gross liabilities transacted in H1 2026 also compares modestly with the $1.537 billion recorded in H1 2025. PRA and FCA are currently consulting on a new UK regime for captive insurers, and suggests it will be worth watching how much captive-related deal activity this generates within the UK, and what knock-on effect that might have on captive arrangements based elsewhere.

item.title: Fairfax’s P&C operating income grows driven by underwriting profit
item.description: Fairfax Financial Holdings Limited’s property and casualty (P&C) insurance and reinsurance operations posted an adjusted operating income of USD 1.11 billion for Q2’26, up slightly from USD 1.13 billion in Q2’25, the same was USD 2.32 billion for H1’26, compared with USD 1.82 billion in H1’25. This growth has been attributed to increased underwriting profit and interest and dividends, partially offset by lower results from associates. The company’s P&C insurance and reinsurance underwriting profit rose to $458.6 million from $426.9 million in Q2’25, and the undiscounted combined ratio improved to 93.1% from 93.3% in the comparative quarter, primarily reflecting growth in business volumes.

item.title: Brit Re drives group premium growth in H1’26 as third-party reinsurance platform expands
item.description: Brit has disclosed that its insurance premiums written increased by 4.4% to $1.77 billion in the first half of 2026, with growth predominantly driven by Brit Re, reflecting the continued expansion of the group’s third-party reinsurance platform. According to Brit, its third-party reinsurance platform is contributing meaningfully to headline growth, with third-party written premiums growing by 69.8% to $150.6 million in H1 2026. Martin Thompson, Group CEO of Brit, commented, “As our Brit Re strategy enters its second full year of deployment, the company continues to gain momentum.

item.title: NHTSA Probes 1.2 Million Tesla Vehicles Over Suspension Failure Risks
item.description: he National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on July 31 it has opened a preliminary investigation into about 1.2 million Tesla vehicles over reports of suspension failures that could cause a loss of vehicle steering control. NHTSA said the suspension failure could leave the vehicle undriveable and require it to be towed. Tesla has previously recalled vehicles over lower lateral link detachments.

item.title: Supply Chain Insurance Is ‘Must-Have’ Cover During Geopolitical Tensions: GlobalData
item.description: Supply chain insurance is seen by businesses as a must-have protection during periods of geopolitical tensions — in order to safeguard their daily commercial operations, according to GlobalData , the London-based data and analytics company. Supply chain insurance (41.1%) is the product expected to see the highest demand due to current geopolitical tensions, with cyber insurance identified as the second most sought-after product, accounting for 20.6% of responses, found a survey conducted by GlobalData. “Organizations are deeply concerned about business continuity amid the cascading risks linked to a highly volatile geopolitical landscape,” commented Beatriz Benito , Iead insurance analyst, GlobalData, in a statement.

item.title: Florida Woman Sentenced in $6 Million Force-Placed Insurance Scheme
item.description: A south Florida woman who was once a licensed insurance producer has been sentenced to spend more than three years in prison and forfeit assets after she pleaded guilty to a leading role in a $6 million property insurance and tax fraud scheme. Lisette Patricio, 64, of Davie, Florida, pleaded guilty in federal court in Miami last month, three years after she was indicted for diverting millions of dollars in premium payments on force-placed policies on homes around the state, court documents show. “The co-conspirators prepared false statement of diligent effort forms fraudulently claiming that three named insurance companies in the State of Florida had declined to issue an insurance policy for the properties with lender-placed insurance policies obtained through Company 1,” prosecutors said in court documents.

item.title: Corgi reaches $4 billion valuation following third funding round in two months
item.description: AI-powered commercial insurance startup  Corgi  has reportedly secured a further extension to its Series B financing, lifting its valuation to  $4 billion  after its third funding round in approximately two months. According to the company, its valuation has increased through a series of funding rounds during 2026: Date Reported valuation Funding event January 2026 $630 million Series A ($108 million) Early May 2026 $1.3 billion Series B ($160 million) Late May 2026 $2.6 billion Series B1 ($106 million) July 2026 $4.0 billion Series B2 extension The company has reportedly raised more than $370 million during 2026. Rapid valuation growth Founded in  2024  by  Chief Executive Officer Nico Laqua  and  Chief Operating Officer Emily Yuan , Corgi provides AI-driven commercial liability insurance for technology companies, offering automated underwriting across cyber, general commercial and AI-related liability risks.

item.title: WTW reports higher second-quarter revenue as AI investment weighs on earnings
item.description: Willis Towers Watson (WTW) reported higher second-quarter revenue but lower net income as acquisition-related costs weighed on earnings, while announcing a $625 million investment to accelerate artificial intelligence and automation across the business. For the quarter, revenue increased 9% year over year to $2.47 billion , with 5% organic revenue growth . “Our strong top- and bottom-line performance this quarter demonstrates the continued progress we’ve made in embedding AI and automation across the business to help us deliver more effective and efficient solutions for our clients.” Hess acknowledged that automation would affect some roles but said the company’s strategy focuses on redeploying employees into higher-value work.

item.title: Porch wants investors to focus on policies, not just premium
item.description: Policy count is becoming the key metric Porch says investors have focused too heavily on reciprocal written premium. “I think people have been very focused on just an RWP, but our economic model is driven through both RWP and policies written.” Porch is now a “Rule of 50” company Excluding its reciprocal insurer, Porch recorded 23% revenue growth and a 30% adjusted EBITDA margin. “Insurance Services, our core largest and fastest growing business stands out even more with 38% revenue growth and a 48% adjusted EBITDA margin this quarter.” Policies are growing faster than premium Reciprocal policies written increased 38% to 59,000, while reciprocal written premium grew 16% to $140 million.

item.title: Arch favors buybacks over expensive M&A
item.description: “While the underwriting environment is increasingly competitive, it is important to note that we are still in the early stages of this softening market.” Arch returned 94% of first-half net income through buybacks Arch repurchased $1.2 billion of shares during the second quarter, bringing first-half repurchases to $1.95 billion. Buybacks currently beat a special dividend Arch issued a special dividend in 2024 when its shares traded at approximately twice book value. “Right now, we’re in the buyback range.” M&A is expensive Arch views acquisitions as a way to add capabilities or scale in strategically important markets—not simply as another outlet for excess capital.

item.title: FCA advances package of equity market transparency reforms
item.description: The FCA has published a package of reforms designed to improve transparency, strengthen access to market-wide information and support confidence in UK equity markets. The package confirms the framework for a future equity consolidated tape, consults on targeted market structure reforms and introduces an interim market activity reporting tool for shares. This package puts us on a path to deliver an equity consolidated tape within 18 months, making market-wide data easier to access and use.

item.title: These Are Sectors Where Seed Rounds Of $5M To $10M Are Clustering This Year
item.description: For this installment, we focused on mid-sized rounds of between $5 million and $10 million, analyzing around 800 global seed financings that closed this year. To illustrate, below we put together a sample set of 15 companies that closed seed rounds in our target range this year: A few standouts include Hint , an AI-powered home management system, Optiml , a developer of software to support real estate decarbonization, and Krane , an AI-enabled construction supply chain platform. Looking across hundreds of financings, however, one forms a clearer image about where the hotspots are clustering.

item.title: $100bn event may not be enough to cause a hard market, say Berenberg analysts
item.description: Adding: “Considering the current financial conditions in the reinsurance market, a $100bn hurricane may be insufficient to cause a hard market; it may be barely enough to halt the pricing declines.” In addition, analysts pinpointed how 2022’s FY global insured catastrophe losses were $150 billion, with Hurricane Ian accounting for $55 billion of the amount, equivalent to 21% of global traditional reinsurance capital. As the reinsurance industry has transitioned into a softening market phase, analysts at Berenberg have indicated that a single $100 billion catastrophe event is unlikely to revert the industry back to a hard market cycle. “Given that H1 2026 insured losses are c30% below their 10-year average level at $46bn, according to Gallagher Re, a single $100bn event (or a series of large events) would not be enough to result in material capital depletion,” Berenberg added.

item.title: US Midwest SCS, wind, hail & tornadoes may rank as a top-10 severe weather loss: Aon
item.description: “With this potential incurred loss figure, the recent Midwest severe weather outbreak may rank near or among the top 10 costliest severe weather events in U.S. A substantial severe weather outbreak in the Midwest of the United States this week is seen as having the potential to result in a top-10 severe weather insurance industry loss event, which would imply the cost could be around $5 billion or higher to the market, according to broker Aon. Aon commented on the potential financial impacts of this weeks severe weather in the United States, “Given the extensive wind, hail, and tornado damage seen in eastern Wisconsin and northern Illinois, total economic and insured losses will likely reach the low-to-mid single-digit billions of USD.

item.title: Kumamoto, Japan earthquake loss expected to be lower than 2016 events’ US $7.7bn: Aon
item.description: Industry losses from the recent magnitude 6.8 earthquake that struck Kumamoto Prefecture are expected to be relatively lower than the devastating 2016 Kumamoto quakes, which caused US $53 billion in economic and $7.7 billion in insured losses, according to broking group Aon. Aon is the latest to provide an event report related to the magnitude 6.8 earthquake that struck the Kumamoto prefecture of Kyushu, Japan on July 28th. In its weekly cat report, Aon said the powerful earthquake that struck southern Japan in late July resulted in at least 35 fatalities and hundreds of injuries, while causing significant property and infrastructural damage across several prefectures.

item.title: Bajaj Finserv Board approves plan to enter reinsurance business
item.description: Bajaj Finserv, an Indian non-banking financial company providing financial services across insurance, fintech, health and asset management, has announced that its board has approved a proposal to establish a reinsurer and enter the reinsurance sector. Bajaj added: “Subject to the approval of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) and other authorities the Board has granted its approval for pursuing re-insurance business through a subsidiary of the Company to be incorporated.” The company’s proposed entry into reinsurance follows a series of changes to its insurance operations. Bajaj said the move would involve pursuing reinsurance activities through a subsidiary, subject to regulatory approvals.

item.title: Banyan Risk launches insurance product for digital asset and emerging risk sector
item.description: “Over the past five years, we’ve also invested heavily in the data and technology that support our underwriting approach, helping us understand these risks and provide a more consistent experience for brokers and clients.” The post Banyan Risk launches insurance product for digital asset and emerging risk sector appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws . Banyan Risk Ltd, a Bermuda-based specialty Managing General Agent (MGA), has announced the launch of a new Digital Assets & Emerging Risks product. “Digital assets and emerging technologies are creating significant opportunities, but they are also producing new and increasingly interconnected risks,” said Peter Horrobin, co-CEO of Banyan Risk Ltd.

item.title: Marsh provides risk and insurance services for Meta’s Texas AI data centre project
item.description: The post Marsh provides risk and insurance services for Meta’s Texas AI data centre project appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws . Marsh, the global insurance broker and risk advisory business, has provided Meta with project risk analysis and insurance services for a new data centre development in Texas, supporting the technology company’s continued expansion of its AI infrastructure. The work relates to Meta’s planned data centre campus in El Paso, Texas, which the company recently announced will be developed through a strategic venture with BlackRock.

item.title: French Insurer AXA’s Profit Rises 2% as Expected, Confident on Outlook
item.description: AXA SA reported first half profit higher than the same period a year ago, as the Paris-based insurer assesses the impact of wildfires currently affecting France and Spain. Last year, the French insurer bought a majority stake in Milan-based insurer Prima Assicurazioni for €500 million [US$574.3 million]. The French insurance group’s underlying earnings came in up 2% to €4.5 billion, the firm said in a statement Friday, meeting estimates.

item.title: Climate Change Made ‘Fire Weather’ in France, Spain More Likely
item.description: Climate change made the weather that fueled Europe’s recent wildfires at least twice as likely in France and at least 20 times as likely in Spain, scientists at the World Weather Attribution group said on Friday. In today’s climate, the weather underlying such intense wildfires can be expected to occur every 20 years in southwestern France and every six years in central Spain, the study found, based on a comparison of historical summer conditions to this year’s. Read more: Insurers Are ‘Actively Evaluating’ New Catastrophe Risks as Europe Burns “Climate change means that the right combination of weather conditions that create a tinderbox and turn it into a disaster happens much more often,” said Friederike Otto, professor of climate science at the Centre for Environmental Policy at Imperial College London and a co-author of the study.

item.description: Okolo of Pikesville, Maryland, to six months incarceration for 10 counts of insurance fraud for acting as an insurance agent without a license. Brown, the jury found that Okolo acted as an insurance agent without a license by selling 11 annuity policies on 10 occasions from 2021 to 2024, receiving more than $88,000 in commissions. This is the second case against Okolo for insurance fraud.

item.title: Markel Insurance launches AI-powered Cortex unit with Bain & Company partnership
item.description: The post Markel Insurance launches AI-powered Cortex unit with Bain & Company partnership appeared first on Insurtech Insights . Markel Insurance has expanded its artificial intelligence strategy with the launch of Cortex , a new business unit developed in partnership with Bain & Company to transform the underwriting and servicing of hard-to-place U.S. The Cortex business unit, launched within Markel’s Wholesale and Specialty division, combines AI technology with the company’s underwriting expertise and proprietary data accumulated over decades.

item.title: Lincoln says its repositioning is over
item.description: Lincoln says its repositioning is over After several years spent rebuilding capital, reducing balance-sheet risk and changing its business mix, Lincoln believes it has reached an inflection point. “The next chapter is no longer about repositioning Lincoln. “This is a capital efficient part of our business that generates attractive earnings and cash flow without the guarantee and an area where we see room for expansion.” Lincoln is choosing profitability over annuity volume RILA sales increased 10%, but management said growth was more moderate because pricing competition has intensified.

item.title: Markel records a $205 million loss at State National
item.description: Markel records a $205 million loss at State National Markel established a $205 million reserve after determining that collateral posted by a bankrupt capacity provider was insufficient to cover expected losses tied to business written through State National. Markel described it as State National’s first substantial credit loss in four decades. “As a result of the work we’ve been doing, it will result in some collateral top-ups for similar lines of business with other reinsurers who are in financially healthy positions.” Markel remains confident in State National Markel acquired State National for approximately $900 million in 2017.

item.title: Ryan’s property employees are producing 11% more quotes
item.description: Property quotes per employee increased 11% Employees across Ryan Specialty Underwriting Managers’ property business produced 11% more quotes per person during the past 12 months. “So the average RSUM on property employees, and this is property employees, not just the underwriters, achieved 11% more quotes per head in the last 12 months than the prior year.” Ryan sees proprietary data—not AI access—as its advantage Ryan is building a proprietary engine to deploy AI within its own controls and train it on internal data. The measure includes all property employees, not only underwriters, and reflects the company’s investments in automating data extraction, structuring, enrichment and rating preparation.
